intro.title: Toggle Visibility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that can show or hide a piece of text with the click of a button. You will learn how to use the useState hook, a core React concept for managing state within a functional component. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and JSX for structuring the user interface. By the end, you will understand how to initialize a boolean state variable, create a handler function to toggle its value, and conditionally render content based on that state.
intro.usecase: Toggling visibility is a fundamental pattern in modern web applications where users need to control what information they see. In dashboards, users frequently toggle between detailed and summary views of data visualizations. Forms often hide optional fields until users click 'Show more options,' reducing initial clutter. Mobile navigation menus slide in and out of view, while accordion FAQs expand only when clicked. Developers implement these patterns daily to create intuitive, space-efficient interfaces that respond to user actions.
